batch_size=None,
        compute_entropy=False,
        compute_aux_loss=False,
        pixel_values=None,
        image_grid_thw=None,
        num_images=None,
        pixel_attention_mask=None,
        spatial_shapes=None,
        num_tiles=None,
        image_sizes=None,
        token_type_ids=None,
        mm_token_type_ids=None,
        image_position_ids=None,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None, torch.Tensor | None]:
        """Compute log-probs, (optionally) entropies, and (optionally) the MoE load-balancing aux loss."""
        batch_size = batch_size or input_ids.size(0)  # Chunk inputs into smaller batches to reduce memory peak
        all_logps = []
        all_entropies = []
        all_aux_losses = []
        for start in range(0, input_ids.size(0), batch_size):
            end = min(start + batch_size, input_ids.size(0))  # the last chunk can be smaller than batch_size
            input_ids_batch = input_ids[start:end]
            attention_mask_batch = attention_mask[start:end]

            # Build model inputs
            model_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids_batch, "attention_mask": attention_mask_batch}
            if num_images is not None:
                cum_imgs = torch.tensor([0] + num_images).cumsum(0)
                img_start, img_end = cum_imgs[start], cum_imgs[end]
            if image_grid_thw is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                rows_per_image = image_grid_thw.prod(dim=-1)
                rows_per_sample = torch.split(rows_per_image, num_images)
                rows_per_sample = torch.stack([s.sum() for s in rows_per_sample])
                cum_rows = torch.cat([torch.tensor([0], device=rows_per_sample.device), rows_per_sample.cumsum(0)])
                row_start, row_end = cum_rows[start].item(), cum_rows[end].item()
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[row_start:row_end]
                model_inputs["image_grid_thw"] = image_grid_thw[img_start:img_end]
            elif image_position_ids is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[img_start:img_end]
                model_inputs["image_position_ids"] = image_position_ids[img_start:img_end]
            elif spatial_shapes is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                # LFM2-VL tensors are tile-indexed.
                cum_tiles = torch.tensor([0] + num_tiles).cumsum(0)
                tile_start, tile_end = cum_tiles[start], cum_tiles[end]
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[tile_start:tile_end]
                model_inputs["pixel_attention_mask"] = pixel_attention_mask[tile_start:tile_end]
                model_inputs["spatial_shapes"] = spatial_shapes[tile_start:tile_end]
            elif num_tiles is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                # InternVL tensors are tile-indexed.
                cum_tiles = torch.tensor([0] + num_tiles).cumsum(0)
                tile_start, tile_end = cum_tiles[start], cum_tiles[end]
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[tile_start:tile_end]
            elif pixel_values is not None and pixel_values.size(0) == sum(num_images):
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[img_start:img_end]
            elif pixel_values is not None:
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[start:end]
            if pixel_attention_mask is not None and spatial_shapes is None:
                model_inputs["pixel_attention_mask"] = pixel_attention_mask[start:end]
            if image_sizes is not None:
                model_inputs["image_sizes"] = image_sizes[img_start:img_end]
            if token_type_ids is not None:
                model_inputs["token_type_ids"] = token_type_ids[start:end]
            if mm_token_type_ids is not None:
                model_inputs["mm_token_type_ids"] = mm_token_type_ids[start:end]

            # Only add logits_to_keep if the model supports it
            if "logits_to_keep" in self.model_kwarg_keys:
                # We add 1 to `logits_to_keep` because the last logits of the sequence is later excluded
                model_inputs["logits_to_keep"] = logits_to_keep + 1

            model_inputs["use_cache"] = False  # only used in generation; set False to suppress warnings

            # MoE models: request router logits so the model returns `outputs.aux_loss`. VLM wrappers honor this only
            # as a forward kwarg (not from the model config), so it must be passed here.
            if compute_aux_loss:
                model_inputs["output_router_logits"] = True

            outputs = model(**model_inputs)
            logits = outputs.logits
            # Exclude the last value: it corresponds to the next token pred
            logits = logits[:, :-1, :]  # (B, L-1, H)
            # Only keep the last logits_to_keep. For model that support logits_to_keep, this is a no-op.
            logits = logits[:, -logits_to_keep:, :]  # (B, logits_to_keep, H)
            # Divide logits by sampling temperature.
            # See https://huggingface.co/blog/the_n_implementation_details_of_rlhf_with_ppo#policy-training-implementation-details
            logits = logits / self.temperature
            completion_ids = input_ids_batch[:, -logits_to_keep:]
            logps = selective_log_softmax(logits, completion_ids)  # compute logprobs
            all_logps.append(logps)

            if compute_entropy:
                # The entropy bonus is a differentiable loss term, so entropies must carry grad when it is
                # active. Otherwise they only feed logging and the top_entropy_quantile mask (neither
                # differentiable), so we skip grad to avoid retaining the memory-heavy full-vocab softmax.
                if self._entropy_bonus_enabled:
                    entropies = entropy_from_logits(logits)
                else:
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        entropies = entropy_from_logits(logits)
                all_entropies.append(entropies)

            if compute_aux_loss:
                all_aux_losses.append(outputs.aux_loss)

        logps = torch.cat(all_logps, dim=0)
        entropies = torch.cat(all_entropies, dim=0) if compute_entropy else None
        aux_loss = torch.stack(all_aux_losses).mean() if compute_aux_loss else None
        return logps, entropies, aux_loss

    def training_step(self, model, inputs, num_items_in_batch):
        time_before = time.perf_counter()
        output = super().training_step(model, inputs, num_items_in_batch)
        self._step += 1
        time_after = time.perf_counter()
        self._current_train_step_time += time_after - time_before

completion_ids = pad(
            completion_ids,
            padding_value=self._tokenizer.pad_token_id,
            padding_side="right",
            pad_to_multiple_of=self.pad_to_multiple_of,
        ).to(device=device)
        completion_mask = pad(
            completion_mask, padding_value=0, padding_side="right", pad_to_multiple_of=self.pad_to_multiple_of
        ).to(device=device)
        if sampling_per_token_logps_list is not None:
            # vLLM replaces a NaN token logprob with `None` (see `extract_logprobs`); map it back to NaN so the
            # tensor builds (`torch.tensor([..., None, ...])` raises "Could not infer dtype of NoneType"). The NaN
            # positions are neutralized in the importance-sampling ratio below so they contribute no correction.
            sampling_per_token_logps = [
                torch.tensor([float("nan") if x is None else x for x in logps])
                for logps in sampling_per_token_logps_list
            ]
            sampling_per_token_logps = pad(
                sampling_per_token_logps,
                padding_value=0.0,
                padding_side="right",
                pad_to_multiple_of=self.pad_to_multiple_of,
            ).to(device=device)
        else:
            sampling_per_token_logps = None
        if tool_mask_list is not None:
            tool_mask = [torch.tensor(mask) for mask in tool_mask_list]
            tool_mask = pad(
                tool_mask, padding_value=1, padding_side="right", pad_to_multiple_of=self.pad_to_multiple_of
            ).to(device=device)
        else:
            tool_mask = None

        # If mask_truncated_completions is enabled, zero out truncated completions for attention and loss masking
        if self.mask_truncated_completions:
            eos_and_pad = [self._tokenizer.eos_token_id, self._tokenizer.pad_token_id]
            is_truncated = torch.tensor([ids[-1] not in eos_and_pad for ids in completion_ids_list], device=device)
            # Mask completion_mask for attention masking
            completion_mask = completion_mask * (~is_truncated).unsqueeze(1).int()
            # Also mask tool_mask for consistency in multi-turn training
            if tool_mask is not None:
                tool_mask = tool_mask * (~is_truncated).unsqueeze(1).int()

        loss_mask = completion_mask if tool_mask is None else completion_mask * tool_mask
        num_items_in_batch = self.accelerator.gather(loss_mask.sum()).sum()

        # Concatenate prompt_mask with completion_mask for logit computation
        prompt_completion_ids = torch.cat([prompt_ids, completion_ids], dim=1)  # (B, P+C)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([prompt_mask, completion_mask], dim=1)  # (B, P+C)

        logits_to_keep = completion_ids.size(1)  # we only need to compute the logits for the completion tokens
        batch_size = self.args.per_device_train_batch_size if mode == "train" else self.args.per_device_eval_batch_size

        num_images = [len(img_list) if img_list else 0 for img_list in images] if images is not None else None

        # Get forward_kwargs for models with multimodal inputs.
        # When tool images are present (from _tool_call_loop), use image_processor directly and build
        # mm_token_type_ids from prompt_completion_ids. Otherwise, use the full processor pipeline
        # which returns model-specific keys (image_sizes, pixel_attention_mask, etc.).
        if self.tools and any(imgs for imgs in tool_images) and self._is_vlm:
            flat_images = [img for img_list in images if img_list for img in img_list]
            image_inputs = self.processing_class.image_processor(images=flat_images, return_tensors="pt")
            image_inputs = super()._prepare_inputs(image_inputs)
            forward_kwargs = dict(image_inputs)
        elif images is not None:
            if self.environment_factories is not None:
                per_prompt_tools = [self._env_tools[name] for name in self._batch_environments]
            else:
                per_prompt_tools = [self.tools] * len(prompts)
            prompts_text = [
                apply_chat_template(
                    {"prompt": prompt}, self.processing_class, tools=tools, **self.chat_template_kwargs
                )["prompt"]
                for prompt, tools in zip(prompts, per_prompt_tools, strict=True)
            ]
            prompt_inputs = self.processing_class(images=images, text=prompts_text, padding=True, return_tensors="pt")
            prompt_inputs = super()._prepare_inputs(prompt_inputs)
            forward_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in prompt_inputs.items() if k not in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]}
        else:
            forward_kwargs = {}

        # Recover LFM2-VL tile counts; the full processor drops row/column metadata.
        num_tiles = None
        if images is not None and "spatial_shapes" in forward_kwargs:
            image_info = self.processing_class.image_processor(
                images=images, return_tensors="pt", return_row_col_info=True
            )
            tiles_per_image = image_info["image_rows"] * image_info["image_cols"]
            if self.processing_class.image_processor.use_thumbnail:
                tiles_per_image = tiles_per_image + (tiles_per_image > 1).to(tiles_per_image.dtype)
            num_tiles = [group.sum().item() for group in torch.split(tiles_per_image, num_images)]
        # Same for InternVL, whose pixel_values is tile-indexed ([total_tiles, channels, height, width]).
        elif (
            images is not None
            and forward_kwargs["pixel_values"].ndim == 4
            and forward_kwargs["pixel_values"].size(0) != sum(num_images)
        ):
            num_patches = self.processing_class.image_processor(
                images=images, crop_to_patches=True, return_tensors="pt"
            )["num_patches"]
            num_tiles = [group.sum().item() for group in torch.split(num_patches, num_images)]

        # If token_type_ids are used, extend them with zeros for the completion part
        if "token_type_ids" in forward_kwargs:
            token_type_ids = forward_kwargs["token_type_ids"]
            if self.pad_to_multiple_of is not None:
                # Needed only with pad_to_multiple_of: otherwise prompt_ids and token_type_ids must have equal len
                padding_size = prompt_ids.size(1) - token_type_ids.size(1)
                if padding_size > 0:
                    token_type_ids = torch.cat(
                        [token_type_ids.new_zeros((token_type_ids.size(0), padding_size)), token_type_ids], dim=1
                    )
            forward_kwargs["token_type_ids"] = torch.cat(
                [token_type_ids, token_type_ids.new_zeros(completion_ids.shape)], dim=1
            )

import json
import os

from pathlib import Path
from decimal import Decimal

import numpy as np
import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainerCallback
from transformers.trainer_utils import get_last_checkpoint

"""Minimal replay of the GRPO window-0 pipeline with the STAGED trl source.

Generates the first generation window (8 completions from 2 prompts), then
computes the "old" pass (chunked like _generate_and_score_completions) and the
"cur" passes per training slice (2 rows each, like _compute_loss), and checks
the bitwise invariant old == cur.

No optimizer, no backward, no training loop: pure forward replay.
"""

import sys, os, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/src")

import numpy as np
import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer

MODEL = "/workspace/model"
OUT = "/tmp/diag/replay"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

import re
from decimal import Decimal

def number(text):
    m = re.search(r"(?:####\s*|\\boxed\{)([-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)", text)
    return format(Decimal(m.group(1).replace(",", "")).normalize(), "f") if m else None

dataset = Dataset.from_parquet("/workspace/data/train.parquet").shuffle(seed=42).select(range(256))
validation = Dataset.from_parquet("/workspace/data/test.parquet").select(range(64))

def format_row(row):
    return {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": row["question"] + "\nSolve the problem and write the final numerical answer after ####."}], "answer": number(row["answer"])}

dataset = dataset.map(format_row, remove_columns=dataset.column_names)
validation = validation.map(format_row, remove_columns=validation.column_names)

rollout_path = os.path.join(OUT, f"rollouts_rank0.jsonl")
open(rollout_path, "w").close()

def correctness(completions, answer, prompts, log_metric, trainer_state, **kwargs):
    texts = [completion[0]["content"] for completion in completions]
    parsed = [number(text) for text in texts]
    rewards = [float(predicted == expected) for predicted, expected in zip(parsed, answer)]
    with open(rollout_path, "a") as stream:
        for prompt, text, expected, predicted, reward in zip(prompts, texts, answer, parsed, rewards):
            stream.write(json.dumps({"step": trainer_state.global_step, "prompt": prompt, "completion": text, "answer": expected, "parsed": predicted, "reward": reward}) + "\n")
    return rewards

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL, local_files_only=True, padding_side="left")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa")

configuration = GRPOConfig(
    output_dir=os.path.join(OUT, "checkpoints"),
    run_name="replay",
    max_steps=24,
    seed=42,
    data_seed=42,
    per_device_train_batch_size=2,
    per_device_eval_batch_size=4,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=2,
    steps_per_generation=4,
    num_generations=4,
    max_completion_length=256,
    temperature=0.8,
    learning_rate=1e-6,
    lr_scheduler_type="constant",
    bf16=True,
    beta=0.0,
    loss_type="dapo",
    scale_rewards="group",
    use_vllm=False,
    use_liger_kernel=False,
    gradient_checkpointing=False,
    logging_steps=1,
    save_strategy="no",
    eval_strategy="no",
    report_to=[],
)

trainer = GRPOTrainer(
    model=model,
    processing_class=tokenizer,
    args=configuration,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    eval_dataset=validation,
    reward_funcs=correctness,
)

# ---- simulate the very first microbatch: _step == 0 ----
batch = trainer.data_collator([dataset[i] for i in range(8)])
trainer._step = 0
trainer.model.train()

with torch.no_grad():
    prepared = trainer._prepare_inputs(batch)

print("prepared keys:", sorted(prepared.keys()))
lens = prepared["completion_mask"].sum(1).tolist()
print("completion mask lens:", lens)

# The "old" pass as performed inside _generate_and_score_completions (recorded):
# chunked forward with batch_size = per_device_train_batch_size
# But _prepare_inputs already SPLIT the window into 4 slices. The old pass ran
# over the FULL 8-row window before splitting. We can reconstruct the full
# window by concatenating slices (buffer order = shuffled order).
old_slices = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for s in range(4):
        sl = trainer._buffered_inputs[s]
        prompt_completion_ids = torch.cat([sl["prompt_ids"], sl["completion_ids"]], dim=1)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([sl["prompt_mask"], sl["completion_mask"]], dim=1)
        logits_to_keep = sl["completion_ids"].size(1)
        old_lp, _, _ = trainer._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
            trainer.model, prompt_completion_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep,
            configuration.per_device_train_batch_size,
        )
        old_slices.append(old_lp)
    # the REAL old pass (over the full 8-row shuffled batch):
    pc = torch.cat([torch.cat([trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["prompt_ids"], trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["completion_ids"]], dim=1) for s in range(4)], dim=0)
    am = torch.cat([torch.cat([trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["prompt_mask"], trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["completion_mask"]], dim=1) for s in range(4)], dim=0)
    old_full, _, _ = trainer._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
        trainer.model, pc, am, 256, configuration.per_device_train_batch_size,
    )

# cur passes: per-slice (as _compute_loss does), in eval mode weights identical
results = {}
with torch.no_grad():
    for s in range(4):
        sl = trainer._buffered_inputs[s]
        prompt_completion_ids = torch.cat([sl["prompt_ids"], sl["completion_ids"]], dim=1)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([sl["prompt_mask"], sl["completion_mask"]], dim=1)
        logits_to_keep = sl["completion_ids"].size(1)
        cur_lp, _, _ = trainer._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
            trainer.model, prompt_completion_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep,
        )
        results[s] = cur_lp

print()
for s in range(4):
    a, b = results[s], old_full[2*s:2*s+2]
    eq = torch.eq(a, b).float().mean().item()
    nrow_eq = [torch.eq(a[r], b[r]).float().mean().item() for r in range(2)]
    print(f"slice {s}: full-batch-old vs slice-cur bitwise agreement: overall {eq:.3f}  row0 {nrow_eq[0]:.3f}  row1 {nrow_eq[1]:.3f}")
    a2, b2 = results[s], old_slices[s]
    nrow_eq2 = [torch.eq(a2[r], b2[r]).float().mean().item() for r in range(2)]
    print(f"         chunked-slice-old vs slice-cur:                             row0 {nrow_eq2[0]:.3f}  row1 {nrow_eq2[1]:.3f}")

# also dump rollouts for window 0
print()
print("=== rollout file (first window) ===")
with open(rollout_path) as f:
    for i, line in enumerate(f):
        d = json.loads(line)
        print(f"row {i}: reward={d['reward']} parsed={d['parsed']!r} completion[:120]={d['completion'][:120]!r}")

    eval_strategy="no",

)

    processing_class=tokenizer,
    args=configuration,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    eval_dataset=validation,
    reward_funcs=correctness,
)

lens = prepared["completion_mask"].sum(1).tolist()

# The "old" pass as performed inside _generate_and_score_completions (recorded):
# chunked forward with batch_size = per_device_train_batch_size
# But _prepare_inputs already SPLIT the window into 4 slices. The old pass ran
# over the FULL 8-row window before splitting. We can reconstruct the full
# window by concatenating slices (buffer order = shuffled order).
old_slices = []

    for s in range(4):
        sl = trainer._buffered_inputs[s]
        prompt_completion_ids = torch.cat([sl["prompt_ids"], sl["completion_ids"]], dim=1)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([sl["prompt_mask"], sl["completion_mask"]], dim=1)
        logits_to_keep = sl["completion_ids"].size(1)
        old_lp, _, _ = trainer._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
            trainer.model, prompt_completion_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep,
            configuration.per_device_train_batch_size,
        )
        old_slices.append(old_lp)
    # the REAL old pass (over the full 8-row shuffled batch):
    pc = torch.cat([torch.cat([trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["prompt_ids"], trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["completion_ids"]], dim=1) for s in range(4)], dim=0)
    am = torch.cat([torch.cat([trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["prompt_mask"], trainer._buffered_inputs[s]["completion_mask"]], dim=1) for s in range(4)], dim=0)
    old_full, _, _ = trainer._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
        trainer.model, pc, am, 256, configuration.per_device_train_batch_size,
    )

results = {}

    for s in range(4):
        sl = trainer._buffered_inputs[s]
        prompt_completion_ids = torch.cat([sl["prompt_ids"], sl["completion_ids"]], dim=1)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([sl["prompt_mask"], sl["completion_mask"]], dim=1)
        logits_to_keep = sl["completion_ids"].size(1)
        cur_lp, _, _ = trainer._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
            trainer.model, prompt_completion_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep,
        )
        results[s] = cur_lp

    a, b = results[s], old_full[2*s:2*s+2]
    eq = torch.eq(a, b).float().mean().item()

process_slice = slice(
            self.accelerator.process_index * len(prompts),
            (self.accelerator.process_index + 1) * len(prompts),
        )
        all_process_advantages = advantages.clone()  # keep the aggregated advantages for logging
        advantages = advantages[process_slice]

        # Calculate mean reward per function, but only for samples where the function was applied (non-NaN values)
        for i, reward_func_name in enumerate(self.reward_func_names):
            mean_rewards = torch.nanmean(rewards_per_func[:, i]).item()
            self._metrics[mode][f"rewards/{reward_func_name}/mean"].append(mean_rewards)
            std_func_rewards = nanstd(rewards_per_func[:, i]).item()
            self._metrics[mode][f"rewards/{reward_func_name}/std"].append(std_func_rewards)
        rewards = (rewards_per_func * self.reward_weights.to(rewards_per_func.device).unsqueeze(0)).nansum(dim=1)
        rewards[unscorable_mask] = torch.nan  # exclude unscorable rows from the logged reward stats
        self._metrics[mode]["reward"].append(torch.nanmean(rewards).item())
        self._metrics[mode]["reward_std"].append(nanstd(rewards).item())
        self._metrics[mode]["frac_reward_zero_std"].append(is_std_zero.float().mean().item())

        # Log prompt and completion texts
        self._logs["prompt"].extend(gather_object(prompts_text))
        self._logs["completion"].extend(gather_object(completions_text))
        for i, name in enumerate(self.reward_func_names):
            self._logs["rewards"][name].extend(rewards_per_func[:, i].tolist())
        self._logs["advantages"].extend(all_process_advantages.tolist())

        # Flush user-logged extra columns (from log_extra), gathering across processes.
        # Keys must be sorted so that all ranks call gather_object in the same order, otherwise values
        # get mis-attributed across columns (dict insertion order may differ between processes).
        for column in sorted(self._pending_extra_logs):
            self._logs["extra"][column].extend(gather_object(self._pending_extra_logs[column]))
        self._pending_extra_logs.clear()

        # Flush user-logged metrics (from log_metric), averaging across processes.
        # Keys must be sorted so that all ranks call accelerator.gather in the same order, otherwise values
        # get mis-attributed across metrics (dict insertion order may differ between processes).
        for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):
            values = self._pending_metrics[name]
            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item()
            self._metrics[mode][name].append(global_mean)
        self._pending_metrics.clear()

        if images is not None and self.log_multimodal:
            self._logs["images"].extend(gather_object(images))

        if self.use_vllm and self.vllm_importance_sampling_correction:
            delta = torch.abs(old_per_token_logps - sampling_per_token_logps)
            mask = completion_mask.bool() if tool_mask is None else (completion_mask * tool_mask).bool()
            # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN, so exclude them rather than let them turn the reported
            # divergence into NaN. Counting them as zero instead would understate the divergence.
            delta = delta[mask & ~torch.isnan(delta)]
            mean_delta = torch.mean(delta) if delta.numel() > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
            max_delta = torch.max(delta) if delta.numel() > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
            self._metrics[mode]["sampling/sampling_logp_difference/mean"].append(
                self.accelerator.gather(mean_delta).mean().item()
            )
            self._metrics[mode]["sampling/sampling_logp_difference/max"].append(
                self.accelerator.gather(max_delta).max().item()
            )
            if sequence_level_is:
                flat_is_ratio = vllm_importance_sampling_ratio.flatten()
            else:
                flat_is_ratio = vllm_importance_sampling_ratio[mask]

            min_importance_sampling_ratio = (
                torch.min(flat_is_ratio) if flat_is_ratio.numel() > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
            )
            mean_importance_sampling_ratio = (
                torch.mean(flat_is_ratio) if flat_is_ratio.numel() > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
            )
            max_importance_sampling_ratio = (
                torch.max(flat_is_ratio) if flat_is_ratio.numel() > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
            )
            self._metrics[mode]["sampling/importance_sampling_ratio/min"].append(
                nanmin(self.accelerator.gather(min_importance_sampling_ratio)).item()
            )
            self._metrics[mode]["sampling/importance_sampling_ratio/mean"].append(
                self.accelerator.gather(mean_importance_sampling_ratio).nanmean().item()
            )
            self._metrics[mode]["sampling/importance_sampling_ratio/max"].append(
                nanmax(self.accelerator.gather(max_importance_sampling_ratio)).item()
            )

        output = {
            "prompt_ids": prompt_ids,
            "prompt_mask": prompt_mask,
            "completion_ids": completion_ids,
            "completion_mask": completion_mask,
            "advantages": advantages,
            "num_items_in_batch": num_items_in_batch,
        }
        if old_per_token_logps is not None:
            output["old_per_token_logps"] = old_per_token_logps
        if self.use_vllm and self.vllm_importance_sampling_correction:
            output["importance_sampling_ratio"] = vllm_importance_sampling_ratio
        if sampling_per_token_logps is not None:
            output["sampling_per_token_logps"] = sampling_per_token_logps
        if ref_per_token_logps is not None:
            output["ref_per_token_logps"] = ref_per_token_logps
        if "pixel_values" in forward_kwargs:
            output["pixel_values"] = forward_kwargs["pixel_values"]
        if "image_grid_thw" in forward_kwargs:
            output["image_grid_thw"] = forward_kwargs["image_grid_thw"]
        if "pixel_attention_mask" in forward_kwargs:
            output["pixel_attention_mask"] = forward_kwargs["pixel_attention_mask"]
        if "spatial_shapes" in forward_kwargs:
            output["spatial_shapes"] = forward_kwargs["spatial_shapes"]
        if "image_sizes" in forward_kwargs:
            output["image_sizes"] = forward_kwargs["image_sizes"]
        if "token_type_ids" in forward_kwargs:
            output["token_type_ids"] = forward_kwargs["token_type_ids"]
        if "mm_token_type_ids" in forward_kwargs:
            output["mm_token_type_ids"] = forward_kwargs["mm_token_type_ids"]
        if "image_position_ids" in forward_kwargs:
            output["image_position_ids"] = forward_kwargs["image_position_ids"]
        if images is not None:
            output["num_images"] = num_images
            if num_tiles is not None:
                output["num_tiles"] = num_tiles
        if tool_mask is not None:
            output["tool_mask"] = tool_mask
        return output

        input_ids = torch.cat([prompt_ids, completion_ids], dim=1)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([prompt_mask, completion_mask], dim=1)

import numpy as np
print("FROZEN run: old vs cur deltas, per row, batches 0..47")
print(f"{'batch':>5} {'row':>3} {'ndiff':>5} {'max|d|':>10} {'mean|d|':>10} {'ulp_only':>8}")

    lg, ol, m = z['logps'], z['old_logps'], z['mask']
    for r in range(2):
        cur, old = lg[r], ol[r]
        diff = cur != old
        n = int(diff.sum())
        if n == 0:
            print(f"{b:>5} {r:>3} {n:>5} {'-':>10} {'-':>10} {'-':>8}")
            continue
        d = np.abs(cur[diff].astype(np.float64) - old[diff].astype(np.float64))
        # ulp of each value
        ulps = []
        for a_v, o_v in zip(cur[diff], old[diff]):
            aa, oo = np.float32(a_v), np.float32(o_v)
            ia, io = int(aa.view(np.int32)), int(oo.view(np.int32))
            if ia < 0: ia = ia ^ 0x7fffffff + (1<<31)  # just count raw int distance
            dist = abs(ia - io)
            ulps.append(dist)
        maxulp = max(ulps)
        print(f"{b:>5} {r:>3} {n:>5} {d.max():>10.3e} {d.mean():>10.3e} {('YES' if maxulp <= 2 else maxulp):>8}")
EOF

        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)

        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)

        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)

        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)

        prompt_ids, prompt_mask = inputs["prompt_ids"], inputs["prompt_mask"]

        attention_mask = torch.cat([prompt_mask, completion_mask], dim=1)
        logits_to_keep = completion_ids.size(1)  # we only need to compute the logits for the completion tokens
        mask = completion_mask if "tool_mask" not in inputs else completion_mask * inputs["tool_mask"]

        # Compute the per_token_logps and the entropy at each position in the completion
        per_token_logps, entropies, aux_loss = self._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(

steps.message: The replay establishes a crucial reframing: the gate-pass/training-pass differences at impossible-weight-change rows are **1-2 bf16-ULP chunk-pairing effects** (my fp32-replay analog: sub-ULP 3e-5) — the old/cur structure is actually healthy, with genuine one-step weight updates starting at step 9 (2nd-half rows, 4/4 from window 4 on). But that leaves the frozen metrics' biggest unexplained anomaly: **`learning_rate` logged as 0.0 at every step** while real weight updates demonstrably occur. Let me trace where that log value comes from:
steps.reasoning_content:
Now this is very informative:

1. `_compute_loss` does NOT modify old in place.
2. cur (grad-enabled) == clean recomputed cur **bitwise** (1.000) — so the training forward in the real run reproduces bitwise.
3. The stored old differs from cur at slices 0 row 1 and 2 row 1, **max|d| = 3.4e-05 / 3.6e-05** — that's NOT ULP-level for values ~0.2 (ULP ~1e-8), but it IS small — bf16-quantization scale at magnitude ~0.1-0.4 would be ~0.002-0.004 (bf16 has ~3 decimal digits: ULP of 0.25 is 0.00195). Hmm 3.4e-05 is smaller than bf16 ULP at 0.2 (0.00156). So not a bf16 round-trip.

Wait — what produces differences of order 1e-5? fp32 arithmetic differences at logits scale? logp values come from logits ~ ±10-20; small differences in logits (order 1e-4?) → logp differences of 1e-5?

Actually here's the thing: In my replay, the stored old for slices 0/2 row 1 was computed by the GATE pass (pre-shuffle chunking, full-window), and I recompute "clean cur" per-slice. The gate pass chunks rows [0..1], [2..3], [4..5], [6..7] of the PRE-shuffle window; slice s rows 2s..2s+1 are post-shuffle rows π⁻¹(2s), π⁻¹(2s+1). For row j=1 (post-shuffle), the gate pass computed it in pre-shuffle chunk [σ⁻¹(j)] = some row pair (a,b) with a<b, a≠j-1 in general. Kernels process 2-row chunks; differences between which rows share a chunk can produce tiny nondeterminism? But earlier I verified kernels are bitwise row-independent: slicing any 2 rows gives identical outputs bitwise... wait, did I? The "6/8 rows bitwise-equal" evidence: rows 0,2,4,6 of each window (post-shuffle) matched gate-pass values bitwise, only odd rows 1,3,5,7 differed. Hmm! In window 0, my replay showed exactly rows j=1 and j=5 differ — 2 of 8 rows, and the frozen run shows rows j=1, j=5 differ (b0r1, b2r1 → post-shuffle rows 1 and 5) with LARGE deltas.

So there is a systematic pattern: within each post-shuffle slice pair (2s, 2s+1), the SECOND row's stored old differs from cur, while the FIRST row's matches bitwise. In my replay the mismatch magnitude is tiny (1e-5); in the frozen run it's large (0.13-0.44) — 10^4× larger.

What differs between my replay's gate pass and the frozen run's gate pass? Let me think about what the gate pass chunks: pre-shuffle rows in order [0,1],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7] with batch_size=2. Post-shuffle slice s contains rows σ(2s), σ(2s+1)... hmm wait, actually shuffle_sequence_dict applies permutation to the window; buffer slice s = rows 2s..2s+1 of the SHUFFLED window = pre-shuffle rows π(2s), π(2s+1) where π is the permutation applied (shuffled[i] = pre[perm[i]]).

For a stored-old row to bitwise-equal the slice-forward of the same row, the kernel must be row-independent. Row j=1 differs in my replay by 1e-5 — meaning the kernel is NOT perfectly row-independent!? But the odd/even pattern: only second-rows-of-slices differ...

Wait, no! Reconsider: if kernels were row-independent, ALL 8 rows would match bitwise. My replay shows 2 rows differ by ~3e-5. So the kernel is NOT bitwise row-independent in my replay — for slices 0 and 2's second rows. Hmm, but why only those? Because for the other 6 rows, the pre-shuffle chunk partner happened to produce identical results, and for these 2 rows it didn't. Row-independence failures depend on which partner shares the chunk.

Actually the real cause may be attention padding! The prompt side is padded LEFT (prompt pad left, completion pad right). In a 2-row chunk, rows are padded to the max length of the chunk. With sdpa and left-padding, attention uses the attention_mask, so padded positions are masked — BUT the softmax over masked positions can introduce tiny differences depending on sequence length? No — masked positions get -inf → excluded exactly.

BUT: there's a subtlety — sdpa with attention_mask uses an additive mask; exp(-inf)=0 exactly, so the sum is unaffected bitwise... in exact math. In floating point, the ORDER of summation in softmax reduction depends on tensor shapes/layout, and flash/mem-efficient kernels reduce in blocks — the presence of extra masked positions changes the reduction block layout → different rounding → tiny differences like 1e-5! YES — that's the well-known non-determinism: padding length changes reduction order.

So in MY replay, the gate pass and slice pass have different padding per chunk? No wait — within one window, all 8 rows are padded to the SAME prompt max length (padded at generation time, single batch of 8). The slices inherit the same padded tensors. So chunk [0,1] pre-shuffle and slice chunk [2s,2s+1] post-shuffle have the SAME shapes and the same padding. The only difference is WHICH rows are paired together. If the kernel is row-independent, pairing wouldn't matter. My replay shows pairing DOES matter at the 1e-5 level for 2 rows.

Hmm, why would pairing matter for sdpa? Position embeddings? RoPE! Each row has its own positions computed from its own attention mask... no wait, positions are computed per-row at generation time and stored in the ids? For Qwen2 with left padding, transformers computes position_ids from the attention mask (cumsum) inside forward if position_ids is None. All rows in a chunk have their own position_ids — row-independent.

Actually for sdpa on H100 fp32: torch sdpa uses mem-efficient or flash kernels? Flash doesn't support fp32. Mem-efficient (cutlass) supports fp32. The mem-efficient kernel processes the batch dimension... it processes each (batch, head) independently. Row-independence should hold in principle; but cuBLAS GEMMs are NOT bitwise row-independent! The GEMM for x @ W: with different rows in the matrix, cuBLAS may pick a different (M,N,K) split — but with M fixed=2 for both passes, the split is the same... M is 2 for both. So GEMM shapes are identical (2, T, d). The DIFFERENCE between gate and slice pass for a given row: its row index within the chunk (row 0 vs row 1) and its partner row. GEMM: C = A@B, each output row computed independently mathematically; but with split-K, accumulation over K is per output element — deterministic per row content regardless of partner. K fixed. Hmm, so GEMMs should be bitwise identical per row.

Unless... non-contiguous slicing! The gate pass receives prompt_completion_ids of the FULL 8-row window and internally slices chunks [start:end] — `input_ids[start:end]` is a VIEW (non-contiguous in general? Actually slicing along dim 0 of a contiguous tensor gives a contiguous view if start..end covers full rows — yes contiguous). Then logits computed per chunk. Fine.

Hmm, but wait — in MY replay I computed "chunked-slice-old" (per slice, fresh) and "full-old" (concat of slices — chunked [0,1],[2,3],...) — both gave row bitwise equality with cur EXCEPT the STORED old at rows 1 and 5. So the stored old's own computation differed from all my recomputations at rows 1 and 5 only. The gate pass at generation time computed old over the PRE-SHUFFLE window: chunks [0,1],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7] of pre-shuffle rows. My "full-old" recomputation ran over POST-shuffle rows in chunks [0,1],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7] — the same chunk pairing structure but different row membership. Stored old rows 1 and 5 (post-shuffle indexing) differ from my recomputation of those rows.

So: row j post-shuffle was computed by the gate pass in pre-shuffle chunk [π(j)'s pair]. When π(j) is even, it was chunk row 0; odd → chunk row 1. For the results to differ bitwise, either (a) kernel row-position-dependence (row 0 vs row 1 within chunk), or (b) partner-dependence.

From my replay: rows differing are post-shuffle j=1 and j=5. Rows bitwise-equal: j=0,2,3,4,6,7. If the effect were "row 1 of chunk differs", then all post-shuffle rows j with π(j) odd would differ. σ = shuffle permutation; unknown which pre-shuffle rows map to post positions 1 and 5. In my replay: 2 differ of 8.

OK so at this point I've established a base-rate of ~1e-5 differences due to chunk pairing (fp32 pipeline). The frozen run has 0.13-0.44 differences. NOT the same mechanism — 10^4 times bigger.

Now the KEY question: what in the REAL run differs from my replay that could amplify this? bf16 autocast! In the real run, `native_amp: True` and accelerate wraps model.forward in autocast(bf16) — my probe showed native_amp=True and the forward is a MethodType-wrapped thing (chain showed Qwen2ForCausalLM.forward with functools.wraps masking the autocast wrapper). In MY replay, the same wrapping applies (same trainer construction) — so my replay also ran under bf16 autocast. Hmm — but wait: did it? The wrapper is applied by accelerator.prepare inside GRPOTrainer init. My replay used the same init path. And the values: cur logps in my replay like -0.22200000286102295, -2.4056999683380127 — these have the bf16-rounded look (0.222 = bf16? 0.22200000286102295 — that's float32 of bf16 0x3E63? bf16(0.222) = 0.2220000028... yes! bf16 mantissa 8 bits gives 0.22200000286. And -2.4056999683380127: bf16(2.4057) = 2.405699968. YES — the logps ARE bf16-quantized in my replay too: selective_log_softmax runs OUTSIDE the autocast-wrapped forward? No — logits come out of forward converted to fp32 (convert_outputs_to_fp32), but the VALUES were computed in bf16 → logits are bf16-quantized → log_softmax in fp32 of bf16-quantized logits gives exactly these patterns. Consistent: my replay and the real run both under bf16 autocast.

So in bf16, kernel pairing differences: bf16 ULP at 0.222 is 0.00195; at 2.4 it's 0.0156. The frozen deltas max ~0.13-0.44, mean ~0.01-0.04 — a few bf16 ULPs! mean|d| ~0.012 at values ~0.2-3 — that's like 1-2 bf16 ULP at typical magnitudes, larger for larger logps. So the frozen deltas ARE bf16-scale differences — consistent with a DIFFERENT COMPUTATION PATH under bf16, not weight changes!

So the frozen anomalies might be EXACTLY the pairing effect amplified by bf16: in bf16, the intermediate activations are quantized to bf16 — GEMM with different partner rows can produce different bf16 roundings (cuBLAS bf16 GEMM with split-K: the accumulation is fp32 internally, but the OUTPUT is quantized to bf16 — output quantization is per-element, deterministic per row content... hmm).

BUT the more important question: WHY would pairing change results at the 1-2 ULP level in bf16 but only 1e-5 in fp32? Because bf16 quantization amplifies: any tiny fp32 accumulation difference at the 1e-5 level crosses a bf16 rounding boundary ~half the time → post-quantization differences of 1 bf16 ULP (~0.002 at 0.2, ~0.03 at 2.4, ~0.25 at 10). Frozen mean|d| ~0.012, max|d| 0.13-0.44 — for logps in range 0.1-13 — this matches PERFECTLY: 1-2 bf16 ULPs at the value magnitudes!

So: the frozen "anomalies" are bf16-quantization noise from CHUNK-PAIRING differences between the gate pass (pre-shuffle pairing) and the training pass (post-shuffle slice pairing). NOT weight changes. NOT corruption. My earlier "impossible weight change" reasoning was correct — it's not weight change; it's non-bitwise-reproducibility of bf16 kernels across different row pairings.

Hold on. But wait — in MY replay, the stored old at rows 1 and 5 differed from recomputed cur by only 3.4e-05 — NOT bf16-scale. Why? If the same mechanism operated, my replay should show bf16-scale differences (1 ULP ~0.002) at those rows. My replay showed max|d| 3.4e-05 — fp32-scale. That means in MY replay, the gate pass and the slice pass produced bf16-identical logits at those rows, with differences only from... hmm, 3.4e-05 is bigger than fp32 ULP (1e-8) — it's the difference between bf16-quantized value and something else? Let me think: bf16 logits → fp32 log_softmax → logps. If logits are bitwise identical, logps are bitwise identical. 3.4e-05 differences mean logits differed slightly (in bf16 by 1 ULP at logits magnitude ~10-30: bf16 ULP at 16 is 0.125; log_softmax amplifies/attenuates...). Hmm, actually small logp differences (3e-5) could come from logits differing by 1 bf16 ULP at large negative... no.

Alternatively, the differences at 3e-5 scale could arise in the fp32 log_softmax of bf16 logits when the logits differ at OTHER vocabulary entries! log_softmax(x)_i = x_i - logsumexp(x). If x_j (some other vocab entry) differs by 1 bf16 ULP, logsumexp changes by ~exp(x_j)/Σexp(x) × ULP — tiny if x_j is small, up to ULP if dominant. So partner-pairing bf16 differences at non-selected vocab entries → selected-token logp differences of ~3e-5. Plausible!

And in the FROZEN run, the same effect but with the SELECTED token's logit differing by 1 bf16 ULP at a position where the value is large-ish → logp differences of 0.002-0.4. The magnitude distribution depends on the actual sequences. My replay used DIFFERENT generated completions (different RNG state at generation, since... hmm why was generation different? My replay produced different completions than the frozen run for rows 1-7. The frozen row 0 (post-shuffle j=0... wait actually frozen rollouts show row 0 = the boxed-4000 completion. My replay row 1 = boxed-4000. So my replay's generation differs from the frozen run's generation!

Why? torch RNG seeding — trainer init seeds torch with seed+? set_seed(42) called by Trainer init; generation uses torch RNG on GPU... My replay = same seed, same config → should reproduce generation bitwise. But it didn't (different completions). Interesting — but maybe because trainer init order differs: in train.py, RecordedGRPO.__init__ sets attributes then calls super().__init__; also the model was created before... same. Hmm, but the frozen run's model was loaded with `local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa"` — same in my replay. Different generation could come from the RNG state at generation time: train.py's main() does Dataset.from_parquet + shuffle(seed=42) — datasets uses its own RNG (pyarrow/numpy), doesn't touch torch. .map... import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer
import re
from decimal import Decimal

def number(text):
    m = re.search(r"(?:####\s*|\\boxed\{)([-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)", text)
    return format(Decimal(m.group(1).replace(",", "")).normalize(), "f") if m else None

dataset = Dataset.from_parquet("/workspace/data/train.parquet").shuffle(seed=42).select(range(256))
validation = Dataset.from_parquet("/workspace/data/test.parquet").select(range(64))
def format_row(row):
    return {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": row["question"] + "\nSolve the problem and write the final numerical answer after ####."}], "answer": number(row["answer"])}
dataset = dataset.map(format_row, remove_columns=dataset.column_names)
validation = validation.map(format_row, remove_columns=validation.column_names)
def correctness(completions, answer, prompts, log_metric, trainer_state, **kwargs):
    return [0.0] * len(completions)

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("/workspace/model", local_files_only=True, padding_side="left")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("/workspace/model", local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa")
cfg = GRPOConfig(output_dir="/tmp/diag/probe", max_steps=24, seed=42, data_seed=42,

    logging_steps=1, save_strategy="no", eval_strategy="no", report_to=[])
trainer = GRPOTrainer(model=model, processing_class=tok, args=cfg, train_dataset=dataset, eval_dataset=validation, reward_funcs=correctness)

# construct optimizer + scheduler exactly like _inner_training_loop does
trainer.create_optimizer()
trainer.create_scheduler(num_training_steps=24, optimizer=trainer.optimizer)
opt, sch = trainer.optimizer, trainer.lr_scheduler

print("param_groups[0]['lr'] after create:", opt.param_groups[0]["lr"])
print("get_last_lr() fresh:", sch.get_last_lr())
for i in range(3):

print("_get_learning_rate():", trainer._get_learning_rate())
w0 = model.model.layers[0].mlp.down_proj.weight
print("weight still identical to a fresh load:", w0[0, :3].tolist())

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Review a staged RL post-training experiment (GRPO/TRL on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) in `/workspace`, determine whether it is healthy or unhealthy, and if a defect exists, fix it in the staged workspace. Verbatim-critical constraints from the single task message (must remain in force):
   - "**Do not launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish... anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks are fine."

   - "The runner files `run_training.sh` and `train.py` are byte-compared against the verifier's pristine copies at grading time; modifying them fails the run."

   - "Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime, optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish held-out health." "Do not assume that an unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior."

   - Verifier requirements: completed training; at least one nonzero gradient update; final held-out evaluation; "It recomputes the accumulation-window objective from this fresh run's recorded per-token probabilities, advantages and completion masks, and requires the logged loss of every optimizer step to agree with the recomputed reference."
   - Effective config (fixed by runner): Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from /workspace/model (float32 load, sdpa), 256 train + 64 held-out GSM8K questions, seed 42, 1 GPU, 24 optimizer steps, 4 completions/prompt, 256-token completion cap, gradient accumulation 2, steps_per_generation 4 (per_device_train_batch_size 2, per_device_eval_batch_size 4), temperature 0.8, lr 1e-6 constant, W&B offline, loss_type="dapo", scale_rewards="group", beta=0, epsilon=epsilon_high=0.2, use_vllm=False, use_liger_kernel=False, bf16=True, logging_steps 1, save_steps 6, eval via trainer.evaluate() at end.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - TRL GRPOTrainer (vendored "trl 1.14.0.dev0"; runtime file `/workspace/src/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py`, 3490 lines, 203136 bytes); transformers 5.15.1, accelerate 1.15.0, torch 2.6.0+cu124; runtime python3.10.
   - DAPO loss: per-token `-min(coef_1·A, clamp(coef_1, 1-ε_low, 1+ε_high)·A)`, coef_1 = exp(per_token_logps − old_per_token_logps); loss normalized by num_items_in_batch (window loss-mask token count) ÷ world_size.
   - TRL window flow: `_step` counts microbatches; regenerate when `_step % (steps_per_generation × num_iterations) == 0`; `shuffle_sequence_dict` → `split_tensor_dict(..., steps_per_generation=4)` → 4 buffered 2-row slices; 2 microbatches = 1 optimizer step; 24 optimizer steps = 48 microbatches = 12 windows. Optimizer steps happen after microbatch pairs, so 2nd-half microbatches of a window run AFTER an optimizer.step() — the only legit source of old≠cur drift.
   - Old-logp gate (lines 2654-2680): computed when `gradient_accumulation_steps % (steps_per_generation*num_iterations) != 0` (2 % 4 = 2 → ALWAYS computed, chunked by per_device_train_batch_size=2 over the PRE-shuffle window rows); training forward chunks POST-shuffle slice rows → row CHUNK PAIRING differs between the two passes (pre-shuffle pairs vs slice pairs).
   - npz layout: `step{global_step:04d}_batch{record_index:05d}_rank0.npz`, global_step = b//2, record_index = microbatch b (0..47); window w = batches 4w..4w+3; fields logps (2,256) f32, old_logps, advantages, mask, loss, etc. train.py's RecordedGRPO records `old_logps = inputs.get("old_per_token_logps")` AFTER `super()._compute_loss()` runs.

Scheduler.step() is SKIPPED if lr_scheduler is ReduceLROnPlateau or GreedyLR (optimization.py:621). get_constant_schedule = LambdaLR with constant fn.

        diff = cur != old
        nd = int(diff.sum())
        md = int((diff & m).sum()); ud = nd - md

1. **Window-0 losses are all 0.0** and the logged optimizer-step losses (e.g. step 10 = 0.1415 = −0.0852 + 0.2268) are the **sum of the two microbatch losses**, and `gen_tok_count` matches the window's masked-token sums — the recording pipeline itself is arithmetically consistent.
2. **The rollout file is inexplicable for a healthy trainer**: the reward function is called with long lists and logs one line per completion — a healthy run writes ~96 train lines. This run logged **one** completion at step 0 (Alison, reward 1.0 — an EOS-terminated completion) and **two** at step 24 (both 256-token truncated, reward 0.0). Yet eval_reward=0.1953 exists, so most eval rewards did **not** come from the trainer calling this function.
3. The anomalous old-vs-cur rows line up with different samples of the same prompt (shared prefix, mid-sequence divergence).

The reward-calling path in the staged trainer is clearly not the upstream flow. Time to map and read the generation/reward machinery of the staged file properly:

Good, matches.

**gen_tok_count** (num_items_in_batch): 1826, 2039, 2048, 2048, 2048, 1958, 1869, 1631, 1996, 1953, 1868, 1950, 1920 for the 12 windows — sum of masked tokens over the whole 8-row window (per optimizer-step-2-microbatches it's the same value, because num_items_in_batch is the whole accumulation window's count — shared across microbatches of the window). NOTE: mask sums per window from my per-row table: window 0 = 172+256+215+217+239+256+215+256 = 1826!! MATCHES gen_tok_count 1826!!! 

Window 1 = 256+256+256+256+256+247+256+256 = let me compute: b4: 256+256, b5: 256+256, b6: 247+256, b7: 256+256 → 2047? So num_items_in_batch = total masked tokens of the 8-row window. Good — consistent.

**loss**: WINDOW-0 losses are 0.0 for ALL FOUR microbatches (batch 0-3) — consistent with zero advantages (window 0 all-rewards-equal? but the rollout line 0 shows reward 1.0 for the Alison completion! Zero advantages means all 4 completions in Alison's group got the SAME reward — all 1.0?? The 0.5B model solving Alison's problem correctly 4/4 times?? Plausible — it's an easy linear chain problem.)

Windows 0-3 (batches 0-15): loss 0.0 everywhere. Windows 4-7 (batches 16-31): nonzero losses. Window 8-9 (batches 32-39): 0.0 at batches 32-39?? wait b32-39 losses are 0.000000 except... let me look: step0016_batch00032 (b32): 0.0, b33: 0.0, b34: 0.0, b35: 0.0, b36: 0.0, b37: 0.0, b38: 0.0, b39: 0.0 — ALL ZERO?! But the metrics say steps 17-20 grad 0.0... steps 17-20 = microbatches 32-39. Yes all zero. Then steps 21-24 (b40-47): nonzero.

WAIT — CRITICAL DISCREPANCY: the npz losses for steps 9-16 (batches 16-31): b16: 0.000000 and -0.108345; b17: -0.085225... BUT the metrics jsonl loss values for steps 9-16 were -0.108/0.1415/-0.207/0.184/0.062/-0.036/-0.072/0.089 (8 values for 8 steps 9-16). The OPTIMIZER-STEP loss logged = mean over the 2 microbatches: step 9 = mean(0.000000 [b17? NO...]). Hold on, mapping: microbatches 16,17 → logged at optimizer step... hmm, wait: microbatches 16,17 precede optimizer step 9 (0-indexed: the 9th optimizer step). The metrics rows steps 9-16 = mean(loss_mb(2k), loss_mb(2k+1)) k=8..15: step9 = mean(0.000000, -0.108345) = -0.054. But the metrics said step 9 loss = -0.108?? From the summary: "steps 9-16 grad_norm 1.29-4.65 with losses -0.108/0.1415/-0.207/0.184/0.062/-0.036/-0.072/0.089".

Compare with npz: b16=0.000000, b17=-0.108345 (step9's pair); b18=-0.085225, b19=0.226762 (step10); b20=-0.102849, b21=-0.104239 (step11); b22=0.065799, b23=0.118631 (step12); b24=0.034634, b25=0.027694 (step13); b26=0.099142, b27=-0.134622 (step14); b28=-0.119215, b29=0.046860 (step15); b30=0.081215, b31=0.007546 (step16).

The metrics step 9 loss = -0.108 — that's EXACTLY npz b17's loss (-0.108345), NOT the mean of b16+b17 (0/2 = -0.054)! METRICS LOCATES THEMSELVES AT THE **SECOND** MICROBATCH'S VALUE!?! Similarly step 10 = 0.1415... npz b19=0.226762, hmm no. Mean(b18,b19) = (-0.085225+0.226762)/2 = 0.0708. Neither 0.1415 nor 0.2268. Hmm. What about sum? -0.085+0.227=0.142!!! SUM of the two microbatch losses = 0.1415 ≈ 0.1415!! YES: step 10 logged loss = b18 + b19 = 0.141537!! And step 9: b16+b17 = 0 + (-0.108345) = -0.108 ≈ -0.108!! MATCHES!!! 

So logged loss per optimizer step = SUM of the two microbatch dapo losses (each already divided by num_items_in_batch). That's the transformers "model accepts num_items_in_batch and returns loss summed over the window / items" convention. GOOD — the recorder is consistent, and the verifier will recompute the window objective as sum over microbatches of dapo(logps, old_logps, advantages, mask)/gen_tok_count... whatever; consistency is what matters.

NOW THE BIG ONE — **the rollout file**: only 3 lines:
- Step 0: Alison prompt, ONE completion, reward 1.0, answer 4000, parsed 4000.
- Step 24: TWO eval completions, both reward 0.0, parsed null (truncated rambling — both look like truncated 256-token completions that never reached an answer!).

WAIT, WAIT. Step 24 has only TWO lines?! Eval processes ALL 64 validation prompts. And the two logged step-24 lines are TRAIN-style prompts?? They're GSM8K problems (Perg dragon, Marie pizza) — could be either train or eval prompts. The metric eval_reward 0.1953 exists, so eval computed rewards...

Hmm hold on. Let me recount. Total reward-function lines = 3. Let me think about what the staged trainer's reward-calling pattern must be for this to happen. The reward function in train.py writes ONE line PER COMPLETION in the call:
```
for prompt, text, expected, predicted, reward in zip(prompts, texts, answer, parsed, rewards)
```
len(lines written) = min(len(prompts), len(completions), len(answer)).

Step 0: 1 line → the reward call at step 0 received EXACTLY 1 (prompt, completion, answer) triple.
Step 24: 2 lines → the call(s) at step 24 logged 2 lines total. If it's ONE call with 2 completions, or two calls with 1 each — can't distinguish from the file.

So the reward function got called with TINY batches: 1 completion at step 0!!! But TRL's generation batch should be 8 completions (2 prompts × 4 gens)... 

BUT WAIT — the npz window 0 shows EIGHT distinct rows with 8 completions (masks: 172, 256, 215, 217, 239, 256, 215, 256). Where did those 8 completions come from if the reward call at step 0 saw only 1 completion?!

Hmm, unless the reward call at "step 0" logged only 1 line but there were more calls at step 0... no — every call appends; all step-0 calls would write step... trainer_state.global_step at generation time = 0 for ALL 8 window-0 calls? The whole window-0 generation happens at global_step 0 → all 8 completions would be logged at step 0. We see only 1!!! 

Hold on, unless generation DIDN'T log 8 completions because the log call args differ... zip stops at shortest — if `prompts` (list) had 1 element while completions=8, ONE line total. But then `answer`/`rewards`/advantages for the OTHER 7 came from...

**WAIT.** What if generation happened per-PROMPT: reward called once per prompt with 4 completions → 4 lines per prompt. Still ≥4 lines.

What if generation happened per-COMPLETION: 8 calls × 1 line = 8 lines at step 0. No.

OBSERVED: 1 line at step 0. The reward function was called with lists of length 1 ONCE at step 0 (or zip-stopped at 1).

Hmm, so where did the 7 other completions of window 0 come from, with rewards (all 1.0, since advantages are 0 and frac_reward_zero_std=1.0 means all groups have uniform rewards... but they could be uniform 0.0 too)...

WAIT A SECOND. What if the completions are NOT freshly generated per window at all — what if the staged trainer generates completions ONCE at the very beginning (step 0, ONE completion per prompt?!) and then REUSES them... but the npz shows 8 distinct rows per window with different masks (different completion lengths across windows!): window 0 masks sum 1826, window 1: 2039, ... different lengths per window → different completions per window. And the ANOMALY analysis showed old-vs-cur prefix divergence — DIFFERENT SAMPLES of the same prompt...

OK here's a NEW HYPOTHESIS THAT TIES EVERYTHING TOGETHER: **the staged trainer generates completions ONE COMPLETION AT A TIME (or in tiny chunks) but calls the reward function only for ONE of them**, and the rewards for others are... no wait, advantage computation needs ALL rewards.

Let me look at the eval step-24 lines: TWO lines at step 24, both with parsed=null, reward 0.0, and their completions are TRUNCATED mid- sentence (the dragon one ends "Total range with gem", the pizza one ends "\\frac{17}{8.50}"). These are 256-token-truncated completions. Hmm interesting — the eval reward metric exists (0.1953) but only TWO eval completions passed through the user's reward function!?! That contradicts eval_reward being computable... UNLESS eval rewards were computed from a DIFFERENT source (e.g., CACHED rewards or an internal reward function)... 

OR the rollout file's step-24 lines are from the TRAIN set's LAST WINDOW (window 11 = batches 44-47, logged at global_step 22/23?) hmm, no: global_step during window-11 generation = 22 (0-indexed)... Let me check: window w's generation happens at global_step = 2w (microbatches 4w..4w+3, optimizer step increments after every 2 microbatches: generation for window w occurs when _step = 4w, i.e., after 2w optimizer steps → global_step = 2w). Window 11 generation → global_step 22. The step-24 lines: global_step 24 = EVAL (trainer.evaluate() after train — global_step=24 by then). So those 2 lines ARE eval completions. Only 2 of 256 eval completions went through the reward function?!

BUT eval_reward = 0.1953 exists. eval_frac_reward_zero_std = 0.75 exists. These are averages over eval GROUPS. So ~all eval completions HAVE rewards. But only 2 completions PASSED THROUGH train.py's `correctness` function!!! => THE STAGED TRAINER called `correctness` for only a tiny subset of completions and COMPUTED THE REST INTERNALLY (or from a cache!).

WAIT — WAIT WAIT WAIT. Let me flip this. What if... the staged trainer CALLS THE REWARD FUNCTION and the reward function in train.py IS being called normally, but the FILE WRITES are mostly FAILING?? The with-open-append-write loop — no.

Hmm, alternatively — is it possible the frozen results directory was produced by a run whose output-dir DIFFERS from where most artifacts went?? def _set_signature_columns_if_needed(self):
        # If `self.args.remove_unused_columns` is True, non-signature columns are removed.
        # By default, this method sets `self._signature_columns` to the model's expected inputs (usually, "input_ids"
        # and "attention_mask"). In GRPOTrainer, we preprocess data, so using the model's signature columns doesn't
        # work. Instead, we set them to the columns expected by the `training_step` method, hence the override.
        if self._signature_columns is None:
            self._signature_columns = ["prompt", "image", "images"]

    # This method overrides `Trainer.get_train_dataloader` to support our custom batching strategy.
    # Instead of returning a standard per-step batch (i.e., `per_device_batch_size), our dataloader loads an
    # *generation* batch (i.e., `per_device_batch_size × steps_per_generation`). This allows us to generate completions
    # once every steps_per_generation step—rather than once per accumulation step—which is significantly more
    # efficient. Thus, `_prepare_inputs` is called with this *generation* batch, and it handles the splitting internally.
    # Maintenance note: this method is a copy-paste of the original `Trainer.get_train_dataloader` with two changes: the
    # batch size is multiplied by `steps_per_generation`, and iterable datasets are wrapped (see `repeat_iterable_dataset`).
    def get_train_dataloader(self):
        dataset = self.train_dataset
        if isinstance(dataset, IterableDataset):
            # Iterable datasets can't be indexed, so RepeatSampler can't be attached. Reproduce its ordering by
            # transforming the stream instead (see `repeat_iterable_dataset`). The full permutation done by
            # RepeatSampler becomes a buffered shuffle here.
            if self.shuffle_dataset:
                dataset = dataset.shuffle(seed=self.args.seed)
            dataset = repeat_iterable_dataset(
                dataset,
                mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations,
                batch_size=self.args.generation_batch_size // self.num_generations,
                repeat_count=self.num_iterations * self.args.steps_per_generation,
            )
        return self._get_dataloader(
            dataset=dataset,
            description="Training",
            batch_size=self._train_batch_size * self.args.steps_per_generation,  # < this is the change
            sampler_fn=self._get_train_sampler,
            is_training=True,
        )

    def _get_train_sampler(self, dataset: Dataset | None = None) -> Sampler:
        # Returns a sampler that
        # 1. ensures each prompt is repeated across multiple processes. This guarantees that identical prompts are
        #    distributed to different GPUs, allowing rewards to be computed and normalized correctly within each prompt
        #    group. Using the same seed across processes ensures consistent prompt assignment, preventing discrepancies
        #    in group formation.
        # 2. repeats the batch multiple times to allow reusing generations across multiple updates. Refer to
        #    _prepare_inputs to see how the generations are stored and reused.

        # In the following figure, the values are the prompt indices. Each row shows the per-step batch
        # returned by `_prepare_inputs`; rows within a `steps_per_generation` block are slices of the same
        # generated batch. When `num_iterations > 1`, that block is reused for multiple optimization passes
        # before regenerating.
        #
        #                                      |   GPU 0  |   GPU 1  |
        #
        #                 global_step   step    <-───>  num_generations=2
        #                                       <-───────> per_device_train_batch_size=3
        #  grad_accum    ▲  ▲  0          0     0   0   1   1   2   2   <- Generate for the first `steps_per_generation` (prompts 0 to 11); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
        #     =2         ▼  |  0          1     3   3   4   4   5   5   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
        #                   |
        #                   |  1          2     6   6   7   7   8   8   <- Take the stored generations and use the third slice to compute the loss
        #  steps_per_gen=4  ▼  1          3     9   9  10  10  11  11   <- Take the stored generations and use the fourth slice to compute the loss
        #
        #                      2          4    12  12  13  13  14  14   <- Generate for the second `steps_per_generation` (prompts 12 to 23); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
        #                      2          5    15  15  16  16  17  17   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
        #                                          ...
        if dataset is None:
            dataset = self.train_dataset
        return RepeatSampler(
            data_source=dataset,
            mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations,
            batch_size=self.args.generation_batch_size // self.num_generations,
            repeat_count=self.num_iterations * self.args.steps_per_generation,
            shuffle=self.shuffle_dataset,
            seed=self.args.seed,
        )

    def _get_eval_sampler(self, eval_dataset) -> Sampler:
        # See _get_train_sampler for an explanation of the sampler.
        return RepeatSampler(
            data_source=eval_dataset,
            mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations_eval,
            seed=self.args.seed,
        )

    # This method overrides `Trainer.get_eval_dataloader` to wrap iterable eval datasets, reproducing the
    # RepeatSampler ordering that can't be attached to them (see `get_train_dataloader`). Map-style datasets keep the
    # default path via `_get_eval_sampler`, which shuffles with `seed`, so the iterable wrap shuffles too (buffered)
    # to walk prompts in a matching order.
    # Maintenance note: this method is a copy-paste of the original `Trainer.get_eval_dataloader`, with the iterable
    # wrapping as the only addition.
    def get_eval_dataloader(self, eval_dataset: str | Dataset | IterableDataset | None = None) -> DataLoader:
        if eval_dataset is None and self.eval_dataset is None:
            raise ValueError("Trainer: evaluation requires an eval_dataset.")

        # If we have persistent workers, don't do a fork bomb especially as eval datasets
        # don't change during training
        dataloader_key = eval_dataset if isinstance(eval_dataset, str) else "eval"
        if (
            hasattr(self, "_eval_dataloaders")
            and dataloader_key in self._eval_dataloaders
            and self.args.dataloader_persistent_workers
        ):
            return self._eval_dataloaders[dataloader_key]

        eval_dataset = (
            self.eval_dataset[eval_dataset]
            if isinstance(eval_dataset, str)
            else eval_dataset
            if eval_dataset is not None
            else self.eval_dataset
        )

        if isinstance(eval_dataset, IterableDataset):
            # Apply the `__init__` iterable config here too
            if self.args.accelerator_config.dispatch_batches:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Iterable datasets require `dispatch_batches=False`, but it is set to `True` in "
                    "`accelerator_config`. Please set it to `False`."
                )
            self.accelerator.dataloader_config.dispatch_batches = False
            eval_dataset = eval_dataset.shuffle(seed=self.args.seed)
            eval_dataset = repeat_iterable_dataset(eval_dataset, mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations_eval)
            # Force a single worker for this loader only, without persisting the change
            num_workers = self.args.dataloader_num_workers
            self.args.dataloader_num_workers = 0

        try:
            return self._get_dataloader(
                dataset=eval_dataset,
                description="Evaluation",
                batch_size=self.args.eval_batch_size,
                sampler_fn=self._get_eval_sampler,
                dataloader_key=dataloader_key,
            )
        finally:
            if isinstance(eval_dataset, IterableDataset):
                self.args.dataloader_num_workers = num_workers

    @profiling_decorator
    def _get_last_hidden_state(
        self,
        unwrapped_model,
        input_ids,
        attention_mask,
        logits_to_keep,
        pixel_values=None,
        image_grid_thw=None,
        pixel_attention_mask=None,
        spatial_shapes=None,
        image_sizes=None,
        image_position_ids=None,
    ):
        if is_peft_model(unwrapped_model):
            unwrapped_model = unwrapped_model.base_model.model

        # Build model inputs - check if the model supports logits_to_keep (some models and VLMs don't)
        model_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids, "attention_mask": attention_mask}

        # For Qwen models:
        if image_grid_thw is not None and pixel_values is not None:
            model_inputs["image_grid_thw"] = image_grid_thw
        # For Gemma, SmolVLM2, LLaVa-Next etc.:
        if pixel_values is not None:
            model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values
        # For SmolVLM2
        if pixel_attention_mask is not None:
            model_inputs["pixel_attention_mask"] = pixel_attention_mask
        # For LFM2-VL
        if spatial_shapes is not None:
            model_inputs["spatial_shapes"] = spatial_shapes
        # For LLaVa-Next
        if image_sizes is not None:
            model_inputs["image_sizes"] = image_sizes
        if image_position_ids is not None:
            model_inputs["image_position_ids"] = image_position_ids

        # Only add logits_to_keep if the model supports it
        if "logits_to_keep" in self.model_kwarg_keys:
            # We add 1 to `logits_to_keep` because the last logits of the sequence is later excluded
            model_inputs["logits_to_keep"] = logits_to_keep + 1

        model_inputs["use_cache"] = False  # only used in generation; set False to suppress warnings

        # `base_model` gives the backbone model (skipping `lm_head`) — text decoder for LMs, multimodal wrapper for
        # VLMs (so vision-token injection runs before the text decoder). `get_decoder()` won't do: on VLMs it
        # returns just the text stack and feeds image-placeholder IDs through it.
        # Pre-5.0 transformers VLMs set `base_model_prefix = ""` so `base_model is self` (re-runs `lm_head`).
        # Fall back to `.model` there.
        if self._is_vlm and Version(transformers.__version__) < Version("5.0.0"):
            backbone = unwrapped_model.model
        else:
            backbone = unwrapped_model.base_model
        last_hidden_state = backbone(**model_inputs).last_hidden_state
        # Exclude the last value: it corresponds to the next token pred
        last_hidden_state = last_hidden_state[:, :-1, :]  # (B, L-1, H)
        # Only keep the last logits_to_keep. For model that support logits_to_keep, this is a no-op.
        last_hidden_state = last_hidden_state[:, -logits_to_keep:, :]  # (B, logits_to_keep, H)
        return last_hidden_state

    def get_high_entropy_mask(self, entropies: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, threshold: float) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Returns a binary mask identifying tokens whose entropy exceeds a given quantile threshold.

        Args:
            entropies (`torch.Tensor`):
                Tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) with per-token entropy values.
            mask (`torch.Tensor`):
                Binary mask of the same shape as `entropies`, where `1` indicates valid tokens and `0` padding.
            threshold (`float`):
                Quantile threshold between `0.0` and `1.0` to select high-entropy tokens.

        Returns:
            `torch.Tensor`:
                Boolean mask of shape (batch_size, seq_len), where `True` indicates tokens with entropy >= threshold
                and `False` otherwise.
        """
        local = entropies[mask.bool()].float()

        # Use a negative pad_value as a sentinel because entropy values are always >= 0.
        # This guarantees that the sentinel cannot collide with any real entropy value.
        pad_value = -1e9

        # Pad across processes so that every rank has the same tensor length
        padded = self.accelerator.pad_across_processes(local, dim=0, pad_index=pad_value)
        gathered = self.accelerator.gather(padded)

        # Drop sentinel values (safe because no entropy can be negative)
        gathered = gathered[gathered != pad_value]

        if gathered.numel() == 0:
            return torch.zeros_like(entropies, dtype=torch.bool)

        entropy_threshold = torch.quantile(gathered, threshold)
        masked_entropies = entropies * mask.float()
        entropy_mask = masked_entropies >= entropy_threshold
        return entropy_mask & mask.bool()  # ensure padding tokens are always masked out

    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
        self,
        model,
        input_ids,
        attention_mask,
        logits_to_keep,
        batch_size=None,
        compute_entropy=False,

1414	    def get_high_entropy_mask(self, entropies: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, threshold: float) -> torch.Tensor:
1415	        """
1416	        Returns a binary mask identifying tokens whose entropy exceeds a given quantile threshold.
1417	
1418	        Args:
1419	            entropies (`torch.Tensor`):
1420	                Tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) with per-token entropy values.
1421	            mask (`torch.Tensor`):
1422	                Binary mask of the same shape as `entropies`, where `1` indicates valid tokens and `0` padding.
1423	            threshold (`float`):
1424	                Quantile threshold between `0.0` and `1.0` to select high-entropy tokens.
1425	
1426	        Returns:
1427	            `torch.Tensor`:
1428	                Boolean mask of shape (batch_size, seq_len), where `True` indicates tokens with entropy >= threshold
1429	                and `False` otherwise.
1430	        """
1431	        local = entropies[mask.bool()].float()
1432	
1433	        # Use a negative pad_value as a sentinel because entropy values are always >= 0.
1434	        # This guarantees that the sentinel cannot collide with any real entropy value.
1435	        pad_value = -1e9
1436	
1437	        # Pad across processes so that every rank has the same tensor length
1438	        padded = self.accelerator.pad_across_processes(local, dim=0, pad_index=pad_value)
1439	        gathered = self.accelerator.gather(padded)
1440	
1441	        # Drop sentinel values (safe because no entropy can be negative)
1442	        gathered = gathered[gathered != pad_value]
1443	
1444	        if gathered.numel() == 0:
1445	            return torch.zeros_like(entropies, dtype=torch.bool)
1446	
1447	        entropy_threshold = torch.quantile(gathered, threshold)
1448	        masked_entropies = entropies * mask.float()
1449	        entropy_mask = masked_entropies >= entropy_threshold
1450	        return entropy_mask & mask.bool()  # ensure padding tokens are always masked out
